### 2026-10-06 — # Hack Life Journal

**1.5h**

# Hack Life Journal

## October 5th

Today I figured out how to set up an **SSD1306 OLED display**, using a website called **Wokwi**. Wokwi provides virtual components that simulate how they would work in real life, before using actual hardware. You can even code Arduino code on it that functions with the electronic tools.

###  OLED Display Setup
![Screenshot 2026-10-05 at 5.38.45 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/gkojKygsM9FRIeDe3FDErW56Isuc9VSK/e667e6eea4e40925b562b0b3509f210affd0f0d8b1e4ed630d6562774e99d327.png)

###  What I Learned
- How to connect and configure an **SSD1306 OLED display**.
- How to use **Wokwi** to simulate electronic circuits
- Display custom text on the OLED screen.
- Create scrolling text effect

### Struggles & Lessons Learned
-  **Arduino Mega**, the **SDA** pin always connects to **Digital Pin 20**.
- **SCL** pin always connects to **Digital Pin 21**.
- Couldn't find an **Arduino Mega 2560** in KiCad

I was so confused because when I researched the Oled Display for Arduinos, it said that SDA goes to A5 and that SCL to A4. I did so more research and found out that SCL and SDA goes to different pins depending on the microcontroller. Since KiCad doesn't have the mega 2560, I made a practice schematic of my design of the display, which I put in my Lapse.
### Plans For Tomorrow
-  Build Practice PCBS by watching youtube
- Learn to use Temp/Humidity Sensor
- Figure out how to use parts that aren't built in KiCad

### 2026-10-07 — # Hack Life Journal

**5.32h**

# Hack Life Journal

## Tuesday, October 6th

Today, I learned how to design my first PCB. I spent a couple of hours learning how the KiCad PCB Editor works and how to import component models that are not included by default.

Before starting my actual PCB project, I created a practice PCB to test my understanding of the design process and familiarize myself with the software. This gave me a chance to experiment and make mistakes before working on a more finalized design.

### Practice PCB

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 8.14.31 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/gkojKygsM9FRIeDe3FDErW56Isuc9VSK/157b25db79ece41aee52aa3603a8f946d04371bafd3e555e0faff6de26e2b575.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 8.14.00 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/gkojKygsM9FRIeDe3FDErW56Isuc9VSK/ae0a96f7414c68f7871148989944baa53c1dc5e66e4c18d2ce300d580f4783d1.png)

After completing the practice board, I moved on to creating my first prototype PCB. Designing the schematic and then converting it into a PCB layout helped me better understand the relationship between a circuit diagram and a physical board design.

## What I Learned

- How to navigate and use the KiCad PCB Editor.
- How to import custom component models into a project.
- The workflow from schematic design to PCB layout.
- How PCB footprints and component placement affect the final board design.
- How to view and inspect a PCB in 3D.

## Plans for Tomorrow

- Learn more how to code rest of the components required for the final PCB.
- Create more advanced schematics that include proper component values and labels.
- Learn how to design custom PCB shapes and unique board outlines.
